open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 request_digest for multipart requests
open_points.text: "every header the kernel sends, names lower-cased and in code-point order, each with its value" and for multipart "the parts in order ... so the boundary is not part of it"
open_points.question: When a multipart request is approved, is the `Content-Type` boundary parameter (and other transport-added header details) part of the approval-covered request or ignored for digest matching?
options: Include the full wire header values exactly as sent (boundary differences invalidate approval)
Normalize multipart `Content-Type` to ignore boundary and hash only the normalized header + part digests
Hash only a fixed kernel-controlled header subset, excluding transport-added/generated headers
open_points.default_guess: Normalize multipart so boundary does not affect `request_digest`, and hash only deterministic kernel-controlled headers.

open_points.subject: A09 handling of 2xx response body when binding has no outputs
open_points.text: A09 rule 3: "a binding without output ports ignores the body." A09 rule 5 table: "status 2xx ... or the body exceeds `service_response_bytes_max`, `stored_value_bytes_max` or the spool ceilings" => `contract_violation`.
open_points.question: If a binding has zero output ports, must the kernel still read and enforce response-body ceilings, or may it ignore the body entirely?
options: Always enforce size ceilings even with zero outputs; oversize is `contract_violation`
Ignore body completely when outputs are empty; no body-size-based failure
Read only up to ceiling and then decide based on whether any output parsing is required
open_points.default_guess: Enforce `service_response_bytes_max` regardless of outputs, as the outcome table states.

open_points.subject: A09 path placeholder reuse semantics
open_points.text: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name" and "An input placed in the path is placed nowhere else"
open_points.question: If the same `{name}` appears multiple times in a path, is that allowed (same input substituted each time) or a manifest mismatch/refusal?
options: Allow repeated placeholders and substitute the same input value at each occurrence
Refuse bindings whose path repeats a placeholder name
Allow only one occurrence unless explicitly declared as multi-use
open_points.default_guess: Allow repeated placeholders, using the same input value in each occurrence.
